prompt: I'm selling on Shopify and want to start offering product bundles to lift my average order value. Customers buy single products today; if I bundle related products with a discount I think I can get them to add more to the cart. I should be able to create and manage bundles myself from the Shopify admin — no developer help needed once it's set up. Two bundle types matter. Fixed: I pick the exact products and the customer buys the whole pack or nothing. Flexible: I define a pool and a count ("pick any 3 from this list") and the customer chooses which items they want. Each bundle should let me pick products or specific variants. The discount should be configurable per bundle. I want to choose between three discount kinds: percentage off the bundle total, a flat amount off, or buy-X-get-Y-free where one of the items is effectively included free. On top of that I want tiered discounts — the more items in the bundle the bigger the cut. For example 2 items 10% off, 3 items 20% off, 4 items 30% off. On the storefront the bundle UI should appear on the product page itself. The customer picks their items (for flexible bundles), sees the discounted total live, and adds the whole bundle to cart in one click — discount applied automatically at checkout. In the admin I want a table of all my bundles, edit any field, enable/disable per bundle, and a count of times each was bought.

intent.desiredOutcome: Merchants create and manage product bundles with tiered discounts; customers configure bundles on product pages and buy them with auto-applied discount codes.
intent.qualityBrief: A polished bundle app handles product/variant lookups without stale caches, generates unique discount codes per bundle type (fixed vs flexible) with correct tiering logic, and displays live totals that never diverge from final checkout price. It must validate that a customer's flexible-bundle selections meet the count requirement before allowing add-to-cart, gracefully handle deleted/unavailable products in existing bundles, and show bundle purchase counts without race conditions on concurrent orders. The admin form should let merchants bulk-edit tiered tiers and preview the discount matrix before saving. The storefront widget must be mobile-responsive, show out-of-stock variants clearly, and disable the add-to-cart button if selection is incomplete or if any item is unavailable.

plan.dataFlow: When a merchant creates or edits a bundle in the admin, the backend persists the bundle definition (members, discount kind, tiers) and then provisions one Shopify automatic discount per tier via discountAutomaticBasicCreate or discountAutomaticBxgyCreate, storing each resulting discount external id in bundle_discount_external_refs. On the storefront, the widget queries the backend for the bundle definition and live variant availability; the customer configures their selection, sees the live discounted total computed server-side, then the widget calls cartCreate with the selected variant merchandise ids and the automatic discount context, delivering an auto-applied discount to checkout. When an order is paid, the backend inspects line items for bundle-tagged purchases and increments the corresponding bundle purchase count atomically. When a product is updated or deleted in Shopify, the backend checks whether any bundle member references that product or variant and marks affected members as unavailable so the widget and admin surface the gap without corrupting the bundle record.

edgeCases: Duplicate orders/paid webhook delivery for the same order — the purchase-count insert must check for an existing row keyed by bundle id and order external id before inserting, treating duplicates as a no-op.

A bundle member product is hard-deleted from the Shopify catalog — the products/delete webhook carries only the product id, so the system must also react to products/update events where product status signals removal, and on widget load must re-validate availability for any member whose product external id matches, marking it unavailable.

A merchant edits a bundle's tiers while a customer has the storefront widget open — the live-total and add-to-cart endpoints always re-read tiers from the database at request time, so the customer's next interaction reflects updated tiers; no stale cart is retroactively modified.

Two simultaneous orders containing the same bundle arrive concurrently — purchase-count inserts must rely on a unique constraint on (bundle_id, order_external_id) so only one row is written and no double-counting occurs under concurrent load.

A customer submits a flexible bundle add-to-cart request with fewer than the required item count due to a client-side bug or retry — the backend re-validates selection count server-side and rejects with an explicit error before any cartCreate call is made.

Shopify returns a userError when provisioning a discount tier during bundle creation (e.g. conflicting automatic discount title) — the system must roll back all locally persisted records for that bundle and surface the Shopify error message to the merchant in the admin form without leaving orphaned discount refs.

hld_v_findings.issue: "payloadPath": "line_item_groups" — this field does not exist on the orders/paid webhook payload. Shopify's order payload exposes a `line_items` array with per-line properties; there is no top-level `line_item_groups` field. The coding agent will read undefined on every paid order, so the `increment-bundle-purchase-count` capability will never correctly identify which bundles were purchased, silently producing zero increments for all orders.
hld_v_findings.fix: Remove the "order line item group ids" signalField and its binding entirely; instead, identify bundle purchases by matching `line_items[].variant_id` (already bound) against the `bundle_components` table, or by reading a bundle-id cart line attribute stored as a line item property at add-to-cart time (source="resolved", resolution="read _bundle_id from line_items[].properties where name='_bundle_id'").

hld_v_findings.issue: "the products/delete webhook carries only the product id; mark all bundle_components referencing that product external id as deleted" — the plan declares NO trigger for `products/delete`. Only `products/update` is wired as a trigger. A deleted product never fires `products/update`, so this edge case describes behavior the system has no mechanism to execute; deleted-product components will remain marked "available" in `bundle_components` indefinitely.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a second external-event trigger for the event "a product is deleted", bound to shopifyTopic `products/delete`, with signalField "product external id" → payloadPath "id", and an idempotency rule of unconditional overwrite keyed by product external id.

hld_v_findings.issue: "op": "product" — this is a single-resource lookup by ID, but the capability's dataNeeds include "search query text" and "pagination cursor", and its description says "search and retrieve products". A single-product-by-ID query cannot satisfy a free-text search with pagination; the op resolves the wrong operation and the coding agent will implement a non-functional product search.
hld_v_findings.fix: Replace the shopifyStep op with the products list/search operation (e.g. `products` query with a `query` argument for text search and `after` cursor for pagination), and update produces/consumes accordingly.

hld_v_findings.issue: "op": "discountAutomaticBasicUpdate" — this step is applied unconditionally for all bundle updates, but BXGY bundles require `discountAutomaticBxgyUpdate`. Calling `discountAutomaticBasicUpdate` on a BXGY discount node will either return a Shopify API error or silently mutate the wrong fields, corrupting the discount configuration for any merchant who edits a BXGY bundle.
hld_v_findings.fix: Branch the second shopifyStep by discount kind: use `discountAutomaticBasicUpdate` for percentage/flat bundles and `discountAutomaticBxgyUpdate` for BXGY bundles; document this conditional in the step's `consumes` field so the coding agent applies the correct mutation.

hld_v_findings.issue: Both `discountAutomaticActivate` and `discountAutomaticDeactivate` are listed as sequential shopifySteps (step 1 then step 2). The coding agent will read this as a two-step protocol and call both ops on every toggle invocation — activating and then immediately deactivating (or vice versa) — leaving the discount in the wrong terminal state every time.
hld_v_findings.fix: Declare only one conditional step: call `discountAutomaticActivate` when desired enabled state is true, or `discountAutomaticDeactivate` when false; document this branching in the step's `consumes` field rather than listing both ops as a sequence.
